description: Scan a repository's source code for compliance and security gaps against the chosen frameworks. Use when the user asks things like 'is this ready to ship?', 'are we GDPR ready?' or 'check this repo for security issues'. By default returns a short list: Gaps first, each with file, line, rule, risk level and a one-line fix, plus counts and what was not covered. To check a fix, call it again with files and rules set to the file and rule you changed. Set format to "full" for the whole Markdown report and JSON. Read-only: it never changes files. Call classify first if you don't know which frameworks apply. Results are for a person to review, never a pass, certification or decision.

all.description: Also include medium-confidence findings, which are held back by default because they are often not real.

files.description: Only list findings in these files or folders, relative to path. Example: ["src/api/users.ts"]. Use after a fix to re-check just that file.

format.description: "summary" keeps the reply small; "full" returns the Markdown report and the JSON.

frameworks.description: Frameworks to check, for example ["gdpr", "owasp-top10"]. Leave out to use lintsure.config.yaml in the repo, or all six if there is none.

limit.description: Most findings to list. The counts always cover everything.

path.description: Folder to scan, absolute or relative to where the server runs. Example: "." for the current project, or "apps/web".

rules.description: Only list findings from these rule ids, for example ["pii.logged"]. Use with files to confirm one fix.

status.description: "gap" for findings the code itself shows, "partial" for ones that need a person to confirm context, or "all".

name: scan
